name: Yaeji
label: XL Recordings
lede: Kathy Yaeji Lee grew up between Queens, Atlanta and Seoul, whispered her way onto dance floors with a Drake remix, then spent a pandemic writing an album about what she wanted to hit with a sledgehammer.

eras.title: Three countries before college
eras.text: Yaeji moved from Flushing to Atlanta at five and to Korea by third grade. Pittsburgh gave her a name for the thing she wanted: an after-hours dance party at Carnegie Mellon called Hot Mass.

years.h: Born in Flushing, Queens, and out the door by five
years.p: Kathy Yaeji Lee is an only child. Atlanta comes first, then South Korea by third grade.
years.xp:
In Korea she changes international schools year by year and, per Wikipedia, finds music mostly through online friendships. A stretch in Japan follows before she returns to the US for college.

The English-Korean split that runs through every Yaeji record starts here: three places, two languages, none of them fully home.

years.h: A Carnegie Mellon dance party teaches her to DJ
years.p: Lee studies conceptual art, East Asian studies and graphic design in Pittsburgh, and credits Hot Mass with her "indoctrination into nightlife".
years.xp: Per Wikipedia she DJs house parties for two years on Traktor, later learns Ableton and starts producing, and goes on air at the college station WRCT. She graduates in 2015 and moves back to New York.

eras.title: Raingurl and a Drake remix
eras.text: Two EPs on Godmode and one Boiler Room set made a graphic-design grad the name every house blog was typing. She sang low, in two languages, over beats built for 2 a.m.

years.h: "New York '93" is the first Yaeji single, out on Godmode
years.p: The title is her birth year. A cover of Mall Grab's "Guap" follows in May.

years.h: Her debut EP collects the first two singles
years.p: Yaeji gathers "New York '93" and the "Guap" cover on Godmode.

yt: Yaeji Boiler Room New York DJ Set
years.h: A Boiler Room set and a Drake rework change her year
years.p: Her first Boiler Room session includes a take on Drake's "Passionfruit", which Godmode later posts officially.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits this set as the moment she gets real attention. The Drake rework ends up on EP2 as a track called "Passionfruit".

yt: Drink I'm Sippin On (Official Music Video)
years.p: The video passes a million views in two weeks, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Pitchfork names the song Best New Track, according to the EP2 article, and it clears 2.5 million views within a month.

years.p: Nick Sylvester produced it with her at Godmode Studio in Los Angeles. "Raingurl" is the lead track, and the BBC Sound of 2018 longlist follows.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, the 18-minute EP blends trap and house, with deep backbeats under her hushed, auto-tuned voice, and takes on displacement, mental health and feminism. Gorilla vs. Bear names it album of the year.

The "Raingurl" video, directed by Yaeji and [[Enayet|113901a2-2036-4a7a-8679-ed91fdd6994e]], is her first with special effects; it arrives on November 16.

eras.title: Coachella, a mixtape, a crowd rush
eras.text: Festival stages, a first record for XL, then lockdown and a Brooklyn show where the crowd came at her.

years.cap: Yaeji DJing at Lowlands Festival, Netherlands, August 2018.
years.h: Coachella, and a single called "One More"
years.p: She plays the desert festival in 2018 and releases "One More" the same year.

years.h: Her first XL release is a mixtape full of guests
years.p: What We Drew is bilingual and gets Pitchfork's 8.0.
years.xp:
Guests include Nappy Nina, Lil Fayo, trenchcoat, Sweet Pea, YonYon, G.L.A.M., Victoria Sin and Shy One. "Waking Up Down" comes out March 10, the title track on March 31.

Metacritic lands on 84, per Wikipedia; it reaches No. 12 on Billboard's World Albums chart.

years.h: Fans rush her at Celebrate Brooklyn
years.p: At BRIC's Celebrate Brooklyn! festival the crowd surges at Yaeji, per Wikipedia. Two months later she releases "Year to Year" and "29" with Oh Hyuk.

eras.title: The hammer
eras.text: The debut album took seven years after "Raingurl". It started from anger, got built with friends from her own scene, and landed at No. 15 on Pitchfork's 2023 year-end list.

years.h: "For Granted" starts the album, louder and more direct
years.p: The first single, with a video, arrives January 17. "Done (Let's Get It)" follows on February 23.

years.src: Wikipedia: With a Hammer · Album of the Year: With A Hammer
years.h: With a Hammer turns rage into 13 songs
years.p: Pitchfork gives it 8.5 and Best New Music, then ranks it No. 15 for the year.
years.xp:
Reviewer Julianne Escobedo Shepherd wrote that it channels "a lifetime's worth of anger into an airy blend of synth-pop, jazz, techno, and ambient." Metacritic and AOTY list 86 and 82 respectively; the Guardian ranked it No. 7.

Producers are Yaeji, [[Enayet|113901a2-2036-4a7a-8679-ed91fdd6994e]], [[Loraine James|5c952c8c-6791-4df4-8dae-f65678e1e900]] and K Wata; Nourished by Time guests on "Happy". Yaeji did the cover art herself.

q: Resting is also resistance. Resting is also revolution.
years.src: Loud and Quiet: Yaeji · NME: Hammer Time · Slant Magazine: Yaeji
years.h: She wanted the hammer to look like her anger
years.p: Yaeji tells Loud and Quiet a sledgehammer felt "so obviously violent and masculine", which was the point.
years.xp:
She brought in Brooklyn session musicians and asked collaborators to do whatever they saw fit. Enayet she calls an extension of herself; K Wata is from her Slink NYC crew.

NME reports the pandemic lockdown left her sitting with feelings she used to avoid, and that the album moves between English and Korean.

eras.title: One more Booboo
eras.text: After the album she went collaborative, with T-Pain, Girl Talk, Teddy Geiger and Underscores all turning up on her singles.

years.h: Features pile up: T-Pain, Girl Talk, Teddy Geiger, Underscores
years.p: Singles include "Pink Ponies" with Geiger, "Believe in Ya" with T-Pain and Girl Talk, and "Booboo2" with Underscores.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, "Booboo2" reaches No. 12 on Billboard Japan's Hot Overseas chart. She also collaborates with E Wata on "Pondeggi" and Balming Tiger on "Wo Ai Ni".
